subject.title: feat: publish plugins with extended-stable releases

question: Should extended-stable plugin releases track every npm-publishable official plugin at the exact core version for each `.33+` release, or should this wait behind the monthly snapshot or covered-plugin policy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100387 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100111?
rationale: The PR is technically reviewable but changes release policy and overlaps with open alternative release-policy branches, so a maintainer should choose the intended extended-stable plugin boundary after the narrow correctness bug is fixed.

options.title: Fix this PR, then choose policy
options.body: Repair the fallback intent bug here and have a release owner compare this all-plugin exact-core path against the open snapshot/covered-plugin path before merge.

options.title: Use the snapshot/covered-plugin path
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers prefer the monthly snapshot or covered-plugin policy from the overlapping open PRs.

options.title: Defer plugin publication
options.body: Keep extended-stable core-only for now and require a later release-design PR for plugin publication and runtime convergence.

recommendation.title: Fix this PR, then choose policy
recommendation.body: Repair the fallback intent bug here and have a release owner compare this all-plugin exact-core path against the open snapshot/covered-plugin path before merge.
